title: SLO-aware prefill shaper and kernel hinting to cut decode tail latency
creator: Nora Patel
description:
Problem: Several production customers are experiencing occasional 95th-99th percentile decode latency spikes during mixed prefill+decode workloads. Root causes identified in traces: (1) admission logic sometimes forms batches with skewed token-length distributions, causing suboptimal kernel selection; (2) prefill requests that trigger large KV cache warmups create transient contention; (3) decode scheduling doesn't prioritize short, latency-sensitive requests when a long-running prefills are in progress.

Goal: Implement an SLO-aware prefill shaping layer that: (a) classifies incoming requests by latency SLAs and expected token cost, (b) shapes admission to avoid blending latency-sensitive short decodes with long prefill-heavy batches, and (c) emits kernel-selection hints (e.g., small-seq optimized kernels, fused attention path toggles) to the runtime for faster tail behavior. The feature should be opt-in by default and controllable per-route in the console.

Scope: admission controller heuristics, admission metadata propagation to serving runtime, changes to prefill/kv warming heuristics, experiments for kernel hint API and fallback policy when hinted kernels are unavailable.
acceptance_criteria: 95th percentile decode latency reduced by >=25% on mixed workloads in lab benchmark relative to baseline
No customer-visible throughput regression (>5% drop) for steady-state large-batch workloads
Config flag per-route exists in runtime + console to enable SLO-aware shaping
Kernel hinting API implemented and falls back gracefully to previous selection when incompatible
E2E canary rollout steps documented and automated in console rollouts
technical_notes: Admission controller will compute a low/medium/high latency bucket per request based on (route-slo, estimated tokens, model-profile). This metadata will be attached to the admission token and stored in the work queue entry.
Introduce ‘prefill priority score’ that decays KV-warm cost for cached prefixes; use it with admission shaping to allow limited concurrent prefills without blocking short decode paths.
Kernel hint payload: {preferred_kernel_family, max_seq_len, attention_mode_hint}. Implemented as small header in RPC and validated by runtime; runtime returns 'accepted'/'rejected' and reason.
Add fast-path heuristics in scheduler: when queue contains >X latency-sensitive items, form a shaped batch capped to Y tokens and use the small-seq optimized kernel family.

Metric instrumentation: add 'admission_bucket', 'kernel_hint_requested', 'kernel_hint_accepted', and per-request 'kv_warm_cost' tags. Add traces linking admission decision to chosen kernel and KV cache misses.
rollout_plan: Stage 1 - Lab: run replay benchmarks with synthetic mixed prefill+decode traces on canary hardware (perf/latency targets validated)
Stage 2 - Internal canary: enable on internal team account at 10% traffic with strict alerting on latency/regressions
Stage 3 - Customer beta: enable opt-in for selected customers with console toggle and collect feedback
Stage 4 - Gradual rollout: ramp to 100% with automated rollback if 95p latency regresses beyond threshold
test_plan: Replay-based perf tests: run 50 replay runs across model profiles (gpt-style, encoder-decoder) measuring p50/p95/p99 for decode and end-to-end prefill+decode
Chaos tests: inject KV cache misses and GPU kernel failures to validate hint fallback
A/B experiments on internal production traffic measuring customer-facing tail latency and throughput
Unit and integration tests for admission metadata propagation and kernel hint handshake
perf_targets: Reduce p95 decode latency by >=25% on mixed workloads
Keep throughput regression <5% at p50 under steady state
Kernel hint acceptance rate >=80% on compatible hardware profiles
risks: Over-shaping could starve high-throughput batch workloads and increase cost per token
Incorrect kernel hints could force slow code-paths on some HW combos; must gracefully fallback
Additional metadata in admission stream adds serialization cost; need microbenchmarks to prove negligible overhead
Console controls increase operational complexity for customers if defaults are not well-tuned
comments: 2026-02-22 - Nora Patel: Initial triage and root-cause summary from production traces. Decided to combine shaping with kernel hinting rather than separate PRs to reduce incompatibility windows.

2026-02-27 - Diego Ramirez: Implemented admission metadata plumbing and simple low/medium/high bucket classifier. Benchmarks show early wins on toy workload (p95 down ~18%). Preparing kernel hint handshake prototype.
2026-03-03 - R&D review (Amina Zhao): Suggested adding decaying prefill priority to avoid cold-start KV storms; requested microbenchmarks for serialization overhead.

2026-03-09 - Diego Ramirez: Kernel hint proto and runtime accept/reject implemented. Added metrics. Running full replay suite; observed a regression in steady-state throughput for very large batches (~6%). Investigating shaping thresholds to avoid regression.

2026-03-13 - PM sync (Liam Chen): Agreed on canary plan and console toggle design. Beta customers identified (finance-analytics and conversational-ops) for opt-in testing. Due date aligned to 2026-03-22 for initial canary rollout docs.
